messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High 5xx rate observed for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 during canary rollout of service-autogen v2.3.14 — detecting spike since 1852107860. Alerting on-call.

sara: I'm seeing ~11% 5xx on the canary pool, latency also up. starting investigation.

sara: @deploy-bot what was included in this deploy? any DB schema changes?
deploy-bot: Release v2.3.14 -> changes: streaming buffer refactor, response preflight check, canary flag=autogen_canary=true (5% traffic). No DB migrations.

mike: I can jump in for infra deep-dive, heading to logs.
sara: quick check: is KV cache warm? codepath touches streaming path that uses kv cache TTL.

leah: I'm seeing errors in the streaming worker logs: "Error: invalid chunk header" from client-stream-processor. repro rate ~1 in 9 requests.

jordan: rolling back the canary flag should be fastest mitigation if the bug is in streaming buffer. can we flip kill-switch?
sara: agree. Leah, gather a short sample of raw logs (request ids) and paste here.

leah: sample request ids: req_8f3a, req_b2d1, req_c0aa. stack traces point to chunkParser.parseLine -> bufferOverflow at stream_chunker.go:214

sara: executing kill-switch:

```bash
# toggle canary off
ops-cli feature toggle set autogen_canary false --env=prod --region=eu-west-1
```

ops-pager: command accepted, propagation initiated (target 5% -> 0%).

incident-bot: Canary kill-switch applied by sara. Traffic percent to canary pool decaying to 0 over 60s.

mike: monitoring metrics... 60s window... 30s: 5xx down to ~6%. 90s: 5xx back to baseline ~0.6% on global, eu-west 1.2%.
sara: marking mitigation: feature flag rollback. moving to triage and root cause.

leah: saving full stack traces and uploading to /mnt/incidents/1852107890/logs.tar.gz. I included the three sample req ids and a small repro script.

jordan: we should do a quick canary replay locally with same payloads to reproduce. Leah, can you share repro snippet?

leah: repro snippet:

```bash
# reproduce streaming boundary
python reproduce_stream.py --req req_8f3a --host eu-west-1.redwood-inference.internal
```
Output: throws bufferOverflow at ~120ms.

mike: customer impact: quick estimate — ~4% of production requests hit canary during rollout; 11% of those hit the failure -> ~0.44% overall failing requests. Small number of paying customers on eu-west region experienced transient 502s, no data loss reported. Notifying support for any inbound tickets.
sara: severity: P2 (partial degradation to subset from rollout). Logging timeline and actions in incident doc.

jordan: will open rollback PR for the streaming buffer change and add feature-flag guarding until fix. assigning to leah for root-cause.

leah: starting root-cause debug, suspect unsafe boundary handling when chunk size==0. adding extra validation.

sara: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m, @mike you take next on-call for monitoring and follow-ups. leave a short runbook for support.
mike: taking handoff. I'll post a short runbook and follow up on postmortem ticket.

mike: runbook (short):
- Monitor eu-west 5xx and latency dashboards (svc/autogen streaming).
- Confirm traffic stays on stable pool.
- Validate rollback PR does not disturb other regions.
- If 5xx rises >2% in 5m, escalate to eng-sre with priority.

sara: thanks team. tagging @ops-pager to notify support and customer success.

ops-pager: Notifying support: "Canary rollout v2.3.14 caused transient 5xx spike in eu-west-1; mitigation applied (canary disabled); monitoring ongoing. Ask customers to retry, no data loss expected."

incident-bot: Incident entry created: INCIDENT-2026-0457 (deploy-canary-eu-west-5xx). Links: /incidents/2026/0457. Severity P2.

mike: I'll schedule a brief post-incident sync in 30m to capture RCA next steps. If anyone sees any lingering regressions ping here. :thumbsup:

leah: pushing WIP patch to branch fix/stream-chunk-guard, PR #5123. requests for postmortem: timeline, traffic percentages, customer visible errors (sample ids) and rollout history.

sara: closing active paging loop, keeping channel open for follow-ups. last check-in now.

sara: <@mike> you have the handoff — please update incident doc status as you see fit.
mike: will do. final note: no rollback of DB schema, only runtime buffer change. rolling artifacts for v2.3.14 will be held until PR #5123 merged and validated.

mike: last_message: monitoring looks stable at 1852108115 — leaving channel for async updates.
